title: Signals & Circuits
subtitle: Computing, spaceflight, cinema, music & future tech

clues.clue: Using only the digits 0 and 1, this number system is the native language of computers.
clues.fact: Eight binary digits make up a single byte.

clues.clue: Ada Lovelace published what's considered the first algorithm for this proposed Charles Babbage machine.
clues.fact: She imagined such machines might one day compose elaborate music.

clues.clue: This British mathematician proposed a test of machine intelligence in a famous 1950 paper.
clues.fact: Turing himself called his test 'the imitation game.'

clues.clue: In 1947, operators taped a moth into the logbook as the first actual 'bug' found in this Harvard computer.
clues.answer: What is the Harvard Mark II?
clues.fact: The logbook page, moth and all, is preserved at the Smithsonian.

clues.clue: Founded in 1970, this Palo Alto lab pioneered the graphical user interface, Ethernet, and laser printing.
clues.fact: A 1979 visit by Steve Jobs helped inspire the Apple Lisa and Macintosh.

clues.clue: In July 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on this.
clues.fact: With no wind on the Moon, his bootprints could last for millions of years.

clues.clue: On April 12, 1961, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first human in space aboard Vostok 1.
clues.fact: His single orbit of Earth lasted about 108 minutes.

clues.clue: Launched by the Soviet Union in October 1957, this was the first artificial satellite.
clues.fact: Its simple radio beeps could be heard by amateur operators around the world.

clues.clue: Launched in 1990, this space telescope was serviced by astronauts in orbit five times.
clues.answer: What is the Hubble Space Telescope?
clues.fact: Corrective optics fixed its flawed main mirror on the first servicing mission in 1993.

clues.clue: Launched in 1977, this NASA probe became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space in 2012.
clues.fact: It carries a Golden Record of sounds and music from Earth.

clues.clue: In 'The Empire Strikes Back,' this Jedi Master tells Luke, 'Do or do not. There is no try.'
clues.fact: Yoda made his first screen appearance in that 1980 film.

clues.clue: HAL 9000 is the calmly menacing shipboard computer in this 1968 Stanley Kubrick film.
clues.fact: Kubrick co-wrote the screenplay with Arthur C. Clarke.

clues.clue: In 'The Matrix,' Neo swallows a pill of this color to learn the truth about reality.
clues.fact: 'Taking the red pill' has become shorthand for facing an eye-opening truth.

clues.clue: Ridley Scott's 1982 film 'Blade Runner' is adapted from a novel by this science fiction author.
clues.fact: The novel is titled 'Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?'

clues.clue: Fritz Lang directed this 1927 silent epic, featuring the robot Maria, about a city divided by class.
clues.fact: Footage long thought lost was rediscovered in Buenos Aires in 2008.

clues.clue: This keyboard instrument has 88 keys in its standard modern form.
clues.fact: Bartolomeo Cristofori invented the piano in Italy around 1700.

clues.clue: Introduced in 1983, this protocol lets synths and computers share notes; its acronym ends in 'Digital Interface.'
clues.fact: MIDI sends performance instructions, not recorded sound.

clues.clue: Played without being touched, this eerie electronic instrument uses two antennas and bears its inventor's name.
clues.fact: Leon Theremin invented it around 1920 in Soviet Russia.

clues.clue: Released in 1970, this compact Moog synthesizer with a built-in keyboard became a stage favorite.
clues.fact: Its portability helped carry synthesizers out of the studio and onto the stage.

clues.clue: This Japanese company's 1980 TR-808 drum machine became a heartbeat of hip-hop and electronic music.
clues.fact: About 12,000 TR-808s were built before production ended in 1983.

clues.clue: Unlike fully immersive VR, this technology overlays digital images onto your view of the real world.
clues.fact: Many AR apps need nothing more than a smartphone's camera and screen.

clues.clue: Quantum computers process information with these units, which can be in a superposition of 0 and 1.
clues.fact: Many quantum chips must be chilled close to absolute zero to work.

clues.clue: Also called additive manufacturing, this process builds objects layer by layer from a digital model.
clues.fact: Engineers have 3D printed rocket engine parts and even entire homes.

clues.clue: Adapted from a bacterial defense system, this gene-editing tool won Doudna and Charpentier a 2020 Nobel.
clues.fact: Bacteria use CRISPR to remember and snip the DNA of invading viruses.

clues.clue: ITER is one of these doughnut-shaped fusion reactors that confine superhot plasma with magnetic fields.
clues.fact: The name is a Russian acronym for a toroidal chamber with magnetic coils.

final_jeopardy.clue: On October 29, 1969, the first message sent over this Pentagon-funded network crashed after just two letters: 'LO.'
final_jeopardy.fact: The intended word was 'LOGIN,' sent from UCLA to the Stanford Research Institute.
